addGuests.handler.ts:52 and :76 use strict equality for identity/dedup, so an existing attendee differing only by case from the submitted guest is inserted as a duplicate; the defect is real though the comment's claim that emails are case-insensitive throughout this handler is not (line 77 is case-sensitive too).

The newly added attendees are created directly from the submitted strings (addGuests.handler.ts:83-102, `email: guest`), so a new guest's stored attendee.email is byte-identical to the value in `guests`; `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541) cannot misroute a newly added guest by casing.

ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts:3-6) has no uniqueness refine and addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 only filters against existing attendees/blacklist, not intra-input duplicates; the Attendee model (schema.prisma:526-539) has no unique constraint on (bookingId,email), so a duplicate email in the request persists duplicate attendee rows.

addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 reads booking.attendees, filters, then inserts at :92-106 with no transaction or unique guard; with no (bookingId,email) unique constraint (schema.prisma:526-539) two concurrent calls for the same guest can both insert duplicates.

The handler filters to `uniqueGuests` before creating attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:74-90) but passes the raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails (line 168); a re-submitted existing attendee stays in `guests`, so email-manager.ts:541 selects AttendeeScheduledEmail and sends a duplicate confirmation. A repo-wide grep for InsightsBookingService finds only the service itself and this test file; there is no remaining `service.findMany(...)` or `where: <conditions>` consumer to migrate, so the asserted broken callers do not exist.

Verified: retryCount is a new column with no index (schema.prisma:1000, only @@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate]) etc. at 1002-1006), and the deleteMany now ORs in an unindexed `retryCount > 1` branch (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43), so the previously index-assisted delete can degrade to a scan; real but performance-only.

The success path correctly does not increment retryCount — it marks the reminder scheduled and stores the sid (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:168-177) — so the comment describes intended behavior and asserts no defect.

True: the same retryCount update block is duplicated in the else branch (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:179-186) and the catch (190-197); this is a code-quality/duplication concern with no behavior difference.

The write uses the stale value read at findMany time (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184/195) rather than an atomic increment; with overlapping runs the increment can be lost, a genuine but narrow concurrency edge case.

The catch block now performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190-197); before this change the catch only logged, so a failing update would now reject the handler inside the for loop, aborting the remaining reminders and no longer returning 200.

Confirmed at mixins.scss:125-131 the newly added `@mixin order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val` (and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) unchanged, while those legacy box-model properties are 1-based (initial 1) versus the 0-based modern `order`. admin-group.js.es6:13 computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so for user_count=50/limit=50 it returns 2 while currentPage (line 8) is 1; showingLast (line 17) is false, the next action (line 30-37) sets offset to 50 and findMembers (models/group.js:23) keeps offset 50, yielding an empty member list labelled '2/2'. A ceiling is needed.

groups_controller.rb:22-26 now unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`, whereas the base file applied limit/offset only for automatic groups (base groups_controller.rb:26-30). The user-facing template group/members.hbs:6 iterates `members` with no next/previous controls (only the admin template got them), so a non-automatic group with more than 50 members now silently shows only the first 50 with no way to reach the rest.

Confirmed: webassets.go:48-49 takes the write lock with defer and never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache before loading, so concurrent callers that already passed the RLock check (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) each re-run the load after acquiring the lock. Effect is limited because the CDN path is disabled (cdn = "" at line 54) leaving only a local file read, so the redundant loads/serialization are small rather than severe.

CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:105-118) does a separate non-transactional CountDevices then INSERT; two concurrent first-time devices when count == limit-1 both pass the check and both insert, so the effective device count exceeds AnonymousDeviceLimit. No unique constraint or locking enforces the cap, so the feature's hard limit is defeated by concurrency.

Returning ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate (client.go:44-47) is the intended behavior of the new device-limit feature, not a demonstrated defect; the comment merely argues the synchronous tag call reduces availability, and its claim that 'every new/unknown device fails' is even contradicted by the cache behavior in impl.go:83-87 (only the first request fails).

In TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit the at-limit call uses DeviceID "keep", which was never inserted, so it only exercises updateDevice's rowsAffected==0 error branch (database.go:95-96). The update-success branch of updateDevice is never invoked by any test (all other stores use deviceLimit 0), so a broken WHERE/SET in the update path would go unnoticed.

tagDeviceUI sets the localCache key at impl.go:87 before CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error, and it returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). Since TagDevice now returns the error (impl.go:147) and Authenticate surfaces ErrDeviceLimitReached (client.go:45), the first over-limit request is denied but poisons the cache, so the same device's retry hits the cache and authenticates — the limit is bypassed.

updateDevice (database.go:95-97) returns ErrDeviceLimitReached purely on rowsAffected==0, conflating 'row not updated' (missing id or updated_at outside the BETWEEN window) with 'limit reached', despite its documented contract of updating an existing device. Impact is small because CreateOrUpdateDevice only reaches updateDevice when count>=limit, but the mislabeled sentinel is treated as fatal by Authenticate (client.go:45).

I18n.locale is a Symbol, not a String: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 receives the value from I18n.locale, and i18n's Config#locale= normalizes to a symbol — spec/controllers/application_controller_spec.rb:106 (pre-existing at base) expects `:en` after `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, which returns the String "en" (config/site_settings.yml:60). So `[locale, :en].uniq` does deduplicate and the claimed duplicate "en"/:en lookup and double file load do not occur.

The cache-invalidation concern is real but narrow: ensure_loaded!/load_locale (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:46-65) never clear @cache (only reload! does, lines 39-43), so with fallbacks now enabled a result cached while a fallback locale was unloaded (e.g. a cached 'translation missing' for a non-:en SiteSetting.default_locale set outside the request cycle) is served stale after that locale is later loaded. The comment's stated mechanism (stale fallback served after the *requested* locale loads) is not reachable because translate loads config.locale before caching (line 68, 71-76).

Confirmed: I18n.translate only loads config.locale (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68) and I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is wired solely into ApplicationController#set_locale (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159). Non-request code translates in a user locale without loading the fallback chain — e.g. app/services/post_alerter.rb:138 `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)` and app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:87 — so Backend::Simple returns 'translation missing' instead of the advertised fallback, defeating the server-side feature outside the request cycle.

server.go:258-262 returns nil,err on Init failure without calling s.cancel(). Because the PR moved search.init ahead of initWatcher (server.go:303-311), search.init can succeed and start its event loop goroutine (search.go:202-213) before initWatcher fails, so the server is discarded while that goroutine keeps running; the error path performs no cleanup. (Note the search goroutine uses context.Background so cancel() alone would not stop it, but initWatcher's s.ctx goroutines would need cancellation.)

bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:144-153) ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu (bleve.go:137-139). The new call at search.go:216 executes in init() right after the watch-event goroutine was started (search.go:207-213), which can run handleEvent -> getOrCreateIndex -> build -> BuildIndex and write the map, so this line can race with / panic on a map write.

bleve.go:88-89 previously held cacheMu.Lock() for the whole BuildIndex body; the PR (bleve.go:137-139) now locks only the cache write, so two callers that both miss GetIndex (bleve.go:60-68) and then call build() can run BuildIndex for the same key simultaneously instead of serialized. getOrCreateIndex (search.go:287-307) has no per-key single-flight, so concurrent builds produce duplicate *bleveIndex instances (one cached, one stale) and, for size > FileThreshold, concurrent bleve.New on the same on-disk directory (bleve.go:96-98). The change introduces true concurrency here.

Each sub-buffer is constructed with only a subset of shards (flusher.py:93, SpansBuffer(shards)), and buffer.py:382-384 computes max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards)) over that subset, so with P processes the aggregate per-cycle fetch/backpressure cap becomes ~P×500 instead of the documented global 500 (options/defaults.py:2716-2721). This behavior change is introduced by the refactor, even though it only manifests when flusher_processes>1.

_create_process_for_shard (flusher.py:127-132) has no caller — grep finds only its definition; the actual restart path uses _create_process_for_shards(flusher.py:259). It is dead code added by this PR.

The docstring at flusher.py:31-32 says 'Creates one process per shard', but lines 60-66 cap processes and distribute shards via modulo, and the CLI default is 1 (consumers/__init__.py:434); this is a docstring/wording mismatch with no behavioral effect.

The click option deliberately sets default=1 and documents 'Defaults to 1' (consumers/__init__.py:434-436), so the None-means-auto fallback is only reachable from tests/factory calls. It is a configuration-default choice rather than a behavior bug, and the default preserves pre-PR behavior.

A value of 0 for --flusher-processes is not a valid configuration (zero processes could never flush), and the 'or' at flusher.py:51 makes it fall back to len(assigned_shards); the suggested None check would itself yield num_processes=0 and crash, so this guards an invalid input with no real use case.

A negative --flusher-processes would indeed break construction (min gives a negative num_processes, empty process_to_shards_map, then KeyError at flusher.py:66), but this requires deliberately misconfigured input; the comment's modulo detail ('for any negative divisor is 0') is also inaccurate since Python's modulo follows the divisor's sign — the KeyError claim holds only because the map is empty.
